workedExamples.question: Given: $3(x - 2) = 2x + 4$. Prove: $x = 10$. Write a two-column proof.
workedExamples.solution:
| Statements | Reasons |
|---|---|
| 1. $3(x - 2) = 2x + 4$ | Given |
| 2. $3x - 6 = 2x + 4$ | Distributive Property |
| 3. $x - 6 = 4$ | Subtraction Property of Equality (subtract $2x$) |
| 4. $x = 10$ | Addition Property of Equality (add 6) |

workedExamples.question: Segments $\overline{AE}$ and $\overline{BD}$ intersect at $M$. Given: $M$ is the midpoint of $\overline{AE}$ and of $\overline{BD}$. Prove: $\overline{AB} \cong \overline{ED}$.
workedExamples.diagram: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 360 290" width="360" height="290"><line x1="60" y1="60" x2="300" y2="240" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="60" y1="240" x2="300" y2="60" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="60" y1="60" x2="60" y2="240" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="300" y1="60" x2="300" y2="240" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="116.4" y1="109.8" x2="123.6" y2="100.2" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"/><line x1="236.4" y1="199.8" x2="243.6" y2="190.2" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"/><line x1="122.0" y1="201.0" x2="114.8" y2="191.4" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"/><line x1="125.2" y1="198.6" x2="118.0" y2="189.0" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"/><line x1="242.0" y1="111.0" x2="234.8" y2="101.4" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"/><line x1="245.2" y1="108.6" x2="238.0" y2="99.0" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="42" y="56" fill="currentColor" font-size="14" font-family="sans-serif">A</text><text x="42" y="254" fill="currentColor" font-size="14" font-family="sans-serif">B</text><text x="306" y="56" fill="currentColor" font-size="14" font-family="sans-serif">D</text><text x="306" y="254" fill="currentColor" font-size="14" font-family="sans-serif">E</text><text x="174" y="132" fill="currentColor" font-size="14" font-family="sans-serif">M</text></svg>
workedExamples.solution:
| Statements | Reasons |
|---|---|
| 1. $M$ is the midpoint of $\overline{AE}$ and $\overline{BD}$ | Given |
| 2. $\overline{AM} \cong \overline{EM}$, $\overline{BM} \cong \overline{DM}$ | Definition of midpoint |
| 3. $\angle AMB \cong \angle EMD$ | Vertical Angles Theorem |
| 4. $\triangle AMB \cong \triangle EMD$ | SAS |
| 5. $\overline{AB} \cong \overline{ED}$ | CPCTC |

The angle in step 3 lies between the two pairs of sides in step 2, so it is the included angle and SAS applies.
